turns.t: Mrs Ingram, I'm Sally, the nurse. I'll do your measurements, then the doctor will go through the scan. Shoes off, please. ~
Oh dear, I hope it's not bad news. I'm so nervous. ~
Weight 54 kilos, height 160 centimetres, BMI 21.1. Blood pressure 120 over 74, pulse 70, temperature 36.5.
That height's gone down, hasn't it? ~
A little, from last year. The doctor will explain. ~
Good morning, Mrs Ingram. It's your bone density review, after the wrist fracture. How have you been?
Fine, in the main. My back has been aching, low down, for some months, since the autumn, I think. Or was it the summer? I'm not sure.
Is it constant, or does it come with movement?
Worse when I bend, or lift, or get out of the car.
Any sudden severe back pain, a particular moment when it started?
No, it crept up. But I did slip on the ice in December, and landed on my bottom.
Any weakness in your legs, numbness, or trouble with your bladder or bowels?
No, none of that.
Have you lost height that you know of?
About three centimetres, I think. My trousers are longer.
Any allergies to medicines?
Alendronate, I came out in a terrible stomach upset and a rash, so they stopped it.
Thank you, that's noted. Medical history?
I broke my wrist, two years ago, and I had an early menopause at forty-three.
Do you smoke?
I gave up in 2010. Twenty a day, for thirty years.
Let me look at your back.
There's tenderness over the lower spine, a mild curve in the upper back, and the movement is stiff.
Doctor, her scan result is in. ~
Thank you, Sally. Mrs Ingram, your bone density scan shows osteoporosis in the spine and the hip. I'd say this is osteoporosis, and your back pain could be from a small compression fracture.
Oh no. A fracture? ~
Possibly, the loss of height fits. I'd like to arrange an X-ray of your spine, to look for fractures, and blood tests, including calcium and vitamin D.
Is it serious? ~
It's treatable. Because the usual tablets upset your stomach, we'll choose a different treatment, such as a yearly infusion. ~
An infusion? ~
A drip, once a year. I'll discuss it with you after the tests. ~
Shall I book the X-ray for tomorrow? ~
Please do. Mrs Ingram, take calcium in your diet, get daily light exercise, and avoid heavy lifting.
I'll try. ~
And if you get sudden severe back pain, or any numbness in your legs, or trouble passing water, come in straight away.
I will. Thank you. ~
